A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPRINT research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and sequential-token results on MATH500, Countdown, and GPQA-Diamond in Table 2 and Figures 4–6, alongside example trajectories in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds total-token results, estimated runtimes, and additional qualitative demonstrations.

M1.justification: The planner–executor inference procedure, dependency-DAG construction, packing rules, filtering threshold, and supervised fine-tuning remain unchanged. Standardizing 'rounds' as 'stages' and adding demonstrations do not introduce new method components.

E1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds a creative-writing demonstration involving a requested 250-word scene, extending the represented tasks beyond STEM. This is one qualitative example; the MATH training data and three quantitative evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged, including the distilled reasoning models, RFT, SoT-chat, SoT-reasoning, and self-consistency. 'Repeated Sampling + Self-consistency' renames the existing parallel-sampling baseline; Appendix A.5 retains its 20-sample procedure.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds total generated tokens as a MATH-500 efficiency metric. Section 4.2 introduces runtime estimation combining time-to-first-token overhead with decoding time. Existing training budgets, benchmark sample sizes, generation settings, and answer-checking procedures are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.3 illustrates parallel subtasks within one solution method through vertical and horizontal asymptote calculations. B.4 adds a creative-writing case study. The existing trajectory examples and analyses of reasoning length, difficulty, and planning stages are retained; no controlled ablation is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The new results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark accuracies and sequential-token values are unchanged. Table 2 adds MATH-500 total-token counts: 11,645 for self-consistency, 1,290 for SoT-chat, 11,538 for SoT-reasoning, 2,880 for RFT, and 3,622 for SPRINT. Section 4.2 newly reports estimated SPRINT/RFT runtimes of 36.92/40.57 seconds overall and 74.47/120.54 seconds for longer chains. B.3–B.4 add qualitative outputs, while v1's approximate 2,890/1,850-token R1 versus distilled-model comparison is omitted.

T1.justification: The dependency definition, stage-assignment recurrence, stage grouping, and parallelization-ratio definition retain their mathematical meaning. The indicator-symbol change is typographical. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: interleaved planning with parallel execution, the trajectory-curation pipeline, and comparable accuracy with reduced sequential tokens. The headline 39%, 45%, and 65% savings claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 expands the explanation of redundant computation in SoT and repeated sampling, and argues that decoding dominates prefilling overhead in its runtime estimate. The hardware limitation remains, now explicitly distinguishing estimated gains from realized wall-clock gains. Appendix B.4 additionally interprets one abbreviated example as evidence of non-STEM generalization.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same prompts, temperatures, token and stage limits, training hyperparameters, hardware, software, and evaluation implementation details. The code-and-data repository link is identical. No additional implementation configuration accompanies the new demonstrations.

R1.justification: The bibliography is pruned from 76 to 44 entries, removing uncited entries such as s1, Hawkeye, and TinyZero, alongside redundant entries. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning against SoT, PASTA, Hogwild! Inference, and APR remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.2 is locally rewritten and reorganized under more specific subheadings, terminology is standardized around 'stages,' and grammar is edited throughout. Two appendix subsections are added, and affiliation and conference-footer text are updated. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a MATH-500 total-token column and revised headers and caption. Some figure captions are refined, and B.3–B.4 add colored trajectory boxes. The seven existing figures retain their substantive visual content; appendix pagination shifts after bibliography pruning.

improvement.justification: The added total-token counts make the efficiency tradeoff clearer: SPRINT uses 3,622 total tokens versus RFT's 2,880 while retaining fewer sequential tokens. Runtime estimates and clearer results discussion add useful context, although measured wall-clock acceleration remains unresolved. The new creative-writing claim has weak support: abbreviated executions assigned to Bran and the noble instead discuss the urchin. Overall, the efficiency-reporting improvements provide a modest net benefit.
